2. Though principal relief sought is to declare the acquisition process initiated under the notification dated 20.02.1975 under Section 3(1) of the Karnataka Acquisition of Land for Grant of House Sites Act, 1972 having been lapsed and for consideration of representation NC: 2023:KHC:34181 dated 04.05.2017 at Annexure-G and to denotify the land being claimed by the petitioner, in view of the law settled down by Apex Court in the case of Indore Development Authority Vs Manoharlal and others reported in (2020)8 SCC 129 and subsequent decisions the issue is no more res integra.
3. sentences.text: The only contention urged by the learned counsel for petitioner is with regard to possession not being taken.

In this regard he refers to order passed by this Court by Division Bench of this Court in W.A.No.112/1993 wherein at paragraph 9 the Division Bench has observed that the authority concerned before taking possession of the land shall consider the representation of the petitioner in the light of the NC: 2023:KHC:34181 observation made therein.

Similar observation is found in the subsequent writ petition filed by father of the petitioner in Writ Petition No.13408/1997 wherein respondents have been directed not to dispossess the petitioner till representation of the petitioner was reconsidered by them.
It is seen that in the order passed by the Assistant Commissioner, Madhugiri produced at Annexure-F it is observed that the possession of the land was taken on 04.08.1993.
Referring to the same, learned counsel for petitioner submits that said contention cannot be countenanced in view of the observation made in writ petition and writ appeal as above.
Thus he submits that the possession continues to remain with the petitioner and the relief sought for needs to be granted.

4. Learned Additional Government Advocate for respondents 1 to 4 referring to the fact that father of the petitioner himself had made representation or application under Section 18 of the Act seeking reference to the competent court for determination of compensation which NC: 2023:KHC:34181 fact is not disputed by petitioner, as already noted above all that petitioner would be entitled is compensation with interest and other statutory benefits.

In that view of the matter reserving liberty to the petitioner to make a representation to the respondent authorities seeking compensation and all statutory benefits which otherwise he is entitled in accordance with law, petition is disposed of.
Such representation shall be made within four weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Respondent authority shall consider the same within twelve weeks from the date of submission of such representation.
All contentions to the extent of claim of compensation by petitioner is left open.
